At Jammu

 Through :- Mr. Sakal Bhushan, Sr. Adv. with

 v.
State of Punjab & Ors.

 Mr. Amit Gupta, Advocate for R-3.

HON'BLE
MR. JUSTICE RAJESH SEKHRI, JUDGE

For the reasons stated in the application coupled with the submissions made at bar,
same is allowed and requirement for filing certified copy of impugned FIR is dispensed with at this stage with a direction to the petitioners to do the needful positively by the next date of hearing.
CrlM No. 1032/2025 stands disposed of.

1. Petitioners have invoked writ jurisdiction of this Court, under Article 226 of Constitution of India,
and inherent jurisdiction vested in this Court in terms of Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 ["BNSS"], for quashment of FIR No. 0275 of 2024, under Sections 406, 420 and 120-B IPC at Police Station, Navi Baradari, Jalandhar, primarily, on the ground that a dispute purely of civil nature is sought to be given a criminal texture by concocting an improbable story,
which is not permissible in law.

sentences.text: As factual narration of the present case would unfurl, petitioner No. 1 is younger brother of private respondent No. 3, petitioner No. 2 is the wife and petitioner No. 3 is son of petitioner No. 1.
The family is embroiled in a property dispute.
3. A company namely, Kartar Goods Private Limited [the company ] came to be established with petitioners and respondent No. 3 as its Directors.
A partnership firm in the name and style of Kartar Freight Carrier [the firm ] was also constituted with respondent No. 3 and petitioner No. 2 as its partners.
Petitioners preferred an application before the National Company Law Tribunal Chandigarh, (NCLT), against respondent No. 3 on the ground of mismanagement of the affairs of the Company.

In the interregnum, however, parties arrived at amicable settlement and executed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 03.10.2022, pursuant to a meeting held on 01.10.2022 at Jammu, whereby properties of the company and the firm were decided to be distributed and it was decided that petitioners will exclusively own the company and respondent No. 3 would resign from the Directorship of the Company and transfer its shares in favour of the petitioners.

Simultaneously,
it was decided that petitioner No. 2 would retire as partner of the firm and relinquish her share in favour of respondent No.
3.
It was also decided that parties shall settle their accounts under the supervision of CA Chopra Malhotra Associates.
4. Pursuant to meeting dated 05.10.2023, time for implementation of MoU dated 03.10.2022 came to be extended till 30.11.2023 for various reasons.

In view of settlement between the parties, a joint application came to be filed before NCLT for withdrawal of the company petition, which came to be dismissed as withdrawn by the NCLT vide order 23.02.2024.
5.

It is alleged in the impugned FIR that petitioner No.2 went to the office of CA Rajinder Chopra,
obtained the share certificates and documents, handed over by respondent No. 3 and petitioners got the shares of respondent No. 3 transferred in their favour.
Petitioner No.1 informed the CA Rajinder Chopra that he would make the payment by cheques and deposit the amount in the account of respondent No. 3.
He sent photos of eight cheques to CA Rajinder Chopra and respondent No. 3 via Whatsapp, but did not make any payment to respondent No. 3 in return.
It is allegation of the complainant respondent No. 3 that petitioners conspired to cheat him and committed criminal breach of trust.

6. According to petitioners, the FIR prima facie does not disclose the commission of any offence,
much less, offences charged against them.

7. The respondents, at the foremost, have questioned jurisdiction of this Court on the premise that occurrence took place within the jurisdiction of Police Station, Navi Baradari, Jalandhar, outside the territorial limits of this Court.
8. The plea, on facts, has been opposed by the official respondents on various grounds urged in the status report.

It is contention of the respondents that petitioners conspired together, took the complainant respondent No. 3 in their confidence and got 51.11% shares of respondent No. 3 Thakur Ashwani Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab & Ors on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78690737/
2 transferred in their names.

entities.text: Thakur Ashwani Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab & Ors
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: However, the amount due in respect of complainant respondent No. 3 i.e. share in the amount of Rs.67,33,124/- and transport Freight of Rs.14.00 lacs i.e. total amounting to Rs.1,07,33,124/- was never paid by the petitioners.
Though petitioners issued cheques in discharge of their legal debt but failed to pay the same, therefore, petitioners committed fraud and criminal breach of trust.
9. Respondent No. 3 has not filed any response to the present petition and his right came to be closed by this Court on 03.06.2025.

10. Heard learned counsels for the parties and perused the record.
11.
Learned counsels for the parties have reiterated their respective stands in the arguments.

12. Mr. Sakal Bhushan, learned Counsel for the petitioners has relied upon Navinchandra N.
Majithia v. State of Maharastra and ors.; (2000) 7 SCC 640 to contend that since a part of the act is alleged to have been done by the petitioners at Jammu, therefore, this Court has jurisdiction to entertain the present petition and grant the relief prayed for.

entities.text:
Navinchandra N.
Majithia v. State of Maharastra and ors.; (2000) 7 SCC 640
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. Allegation against the petitioners is that it was decided between the parties that respondent no. 3 will transfer his share holding in the company in favour of the petitioners and in consideration,
petitioners will pay an amount of Rs.67,33,124/- and Rs.14.00 lacs as transport freight i.e. total Rs.1,07,33,124/- to respondent No. 3.

It was also decided that respondent No. 3 will hand over share certificates and documents regarding transfer of shares to CA Rajinder Chopra and similarly petitioner No. 1 will give the aforesaid money to CA Rajinder Chopra.
It is alleged that respondent No. 3 handed over the share certificates and share transfer documents to CA Rajinder Chopra.

Petitioner No. 1 informed CA Rajinder Chopra that he would make the payment by cheques and would deposit the amount in the account of Respondent No. 3 and later he sent photos of eight cheques to CA Rajinder Chopra and respondent no. 3 via Whatsapp.
It is further alleged that petitioner No. 2 later went to the office of CA Rajinder Chopra and took away the share certificates and share transfer documents.
It is alleged that though the petitioners got the shares of respondent No. 3 transferred in their favour but they did not make any payment to him in return.
According to respondent No. 3, the complainant, petitioners had conspired to cheat him by criminal breach of trust.

14. In Navinchandra N. Majithia (supra), the appellant filed a writ petition in State of Maharastra for quashment of a complant filed in the State of Meghalaya and Hon ble Supreme Court clarified that mere registration of an FIR in a particular State is not the sole criterion to decide that no cause of action has arisen within the territorial limits of another State.

It was observed that if any part of cause of action has arisen within the territorial jurisdiction of a particular High Court, the said High Court shall have the jurisdiction to entertain the petition.

It came to be noticed by the Apex Court that since a large number of events had taken place at Bombay in respect of the allegations contained in the FIR at Shilong, therefore, Bombay High Court had the jurisdiction.

15. Relevant excerpts captured in paras 43 and 44 are reproduced below, for the ease of reference:

3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We make it clear that the mere fact that FIR was registered in a particular State is not the sole criterion to decide that no cause of action has arisen even partly within the territorial limits of jurisdiction of another State.

Nor are we to be understood that any person can create a fake cause of action or even concoct one by simply jutting into the territorial limits of another State or by making a sojourn or even a permanent residence therein.
The place of residence of the person moving a High Court is not the criterion to determine the contours of the cause of action in that particular writ petition.
The High Court before which the writ petition is filed must ascertain whether any part of the cause of action has arisen within the territorial limits of its jurisdiction.
It depends upon the facts in each case.
44. In the present case, a large number of events have taken place at Bombay in respect of the allegations contained in the FIR registered at Shillong.
If the averments in the writ petition are correct then the major portion of the facts which led to the registering of the FIR have taken place at Bombay.
It is unnecessary to repeat those events over again as Mohapatra, J. has adverted to them with precision and the needed details."

16. If we approach the present case with the aforesaid principle of law enunciated by Hon ble Supreme Court, it is evident that following events have admittedly taken place at Jammu:
i.

The MoU dated 03.10.2022 has admittedly been executed and notarized in Jammu,
within the territorial limits of this Court.

It is as per Clause (6) of the MoU that petitioners accused were to pay the amount equivalent to the value of shares, in consideration of transfer of the share holding of Kartar Goods Pvt. Ltd. in their favour, which according to the complainant respondent no. 3, they have failed to pay and instead petitioner No. 1 sent photos of certain cheques on Whatsapp without actual payment, thus, committing the offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust.

It is case of the investigating agency that aforesaid offences have arisen out of breach of said MoU, which is executed and notarized at Jammu;
ii.

The cheques in question are alleged to have been issued and sent from Jammu,
though received by the complainant respondent No. 3 at Jalandhar.

As per Section 202 BNSS, in offences, of which cheating is a component, if deception is practised by means of electronic communications, they can be enquired into or tried by any Court within whose local jurisdiction such electronic communication is sent "or" was received.

It is evident from the conjunction "or" providing two alternatives that both the places, within whose jurisdiction the communication is sent or received, shall have the jurisdiction to enquire into and try the offence.

I am fortified in my opinion by Lee Kun Hee, President, Samsung Corporation, South Korea and other v. State of U. P. and others; (2012) 3 SCC 132, relied by learned counsel for the petitioners;
iii.

As per the preliminary verification, which forms part of the impugned FIR, the aforesaid cheques are also drawn on HDFC Bank, Branch, Karan Market, Jammu i.e. within local limits of this Court Thakur Ashwani Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab & Ors on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78690737/
4 and allegedly sent by petitioner No. 1 through Whatsapp from Jammu to CA Rajinder Chopra in Jalandhar.

entities.text: Thakur Ashwani Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: iv . Company has a branch office in Gandhi Nagar, Jammu; and v. MoU, breach whereof is alleged in the FIR pertains to various properties including properties situate at Jammu and Srinagar, again within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court.

17. It is manifest from the afore-noted events that a part of cause of action has arisen within the territorial limits of this Court and therefore this Court has jurisdiction to entertain the petition and grant the relief prayed for.

18. On facts, petitioners are aggrieved of FIR on the predominant premise that respondent no. 3 has concocted a false and improbable story to convert a dispute, purely of civil nature, into a criminal prosecution, which is not permissible in law.
19. Prima facie, case for indulgence is made out.

20. Admit.
21.

Post admission notice is waived by Mrs. Sagira Jaffer, Assisting counsel appearing vice Mrs.
Monika Kohli, learned Sr. AAG on behalf of respondents No. 1 and 2 and Mr. Amit Gupta, Advocate on behalf of respondent No. 3.
They seek and are granted four weeks to file counter affidavit.
Meanwhile, investigation of the impugned FIR shall stay.

(Rajesh Sekhri) Judge JAMMU 04.06.2025 Paramjeet Thakur Ashwani Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab & Ors on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78690737/
